title: Scanner fingerprint normalization + SIEM ingest proposal
summary: Working proposal for normalizing multi-scanner output into a consistent fingerprint, mapping canonical fields for SIEM ingestion, and RBAC/audit log requirements to support automated evidence collection and SLA enforcement.
body:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a pragmatic normalization layer between our scanners (Snyk, Trivy, OSV feeds, internal dependency-scan agent) and the SIEM/Remediation tracking pipeline. Goals: de-duplicate noisy findings, preserve scanner provenance, enable deterministic SLA calculations and auditable remediation trails compatible with RBAC v2 controls.

Scope:
- Input scanners: Snyk (container & deps), Trivy, Clair (registry scans), oss-audit internal agent, and OSV pushfeed.
- Outputs: canonical vulnerability events for SIEM (redwood.vuln.scan.event), remediation audit events (redwood.vuln.remediation.audit), and evidence artifacts stored in evidence-bucket.
- Excludes: source code SCA signals that require code-owner workflows (tracked separately).

Key problems observed:
- Same underlying issue appears as different IDs across scanners (e.g., GHSA vs CVE vs internal advisory) leading to duplicated tickets and SLA resets.
- Inconsistent asset identification (image digest vs deployment name vs host id) reduces ability to correlate across infrastructure.
- Remediation evidence is ad-hoc (screenshots, patch PR links) with no standardized metadata to attach to audit logs.

Normalization design (high level):
1) Identifier precedence (ordered): CVE > GHSA/GHSA-like advisory > OSV ID > scanner-native ID. When multiple IDs are present, store primary_id = earliest authoritative public ID (prefer CVE).
2) Canonical asset mapping: convert scanner asset to (asset_type, asset_id) where asset_type in {container_image, pkg, host, k8s_resource}. Asset_id prefers immutable identifiers: image digest (sha256:...), package purl, host-id. If scanner only provides name, resolve via registry/CMDB lookup and add resolved_id.
3) Fingerprint generation: compute fingerprint = sha256( canonical_key ) where canonical_key is the concatenation of: primary_id | asset_type | asset_id | normalized_location (file/path or k8s container path) | vulnerability_context_hash. vulnerability_context_hash is a compact hash of short context fields (line numbers removed for non-source findings) to avoid noise from whitespace or stack order.
4) Confidence scoring: produce a small vector (scanner_presence_count, earliest_report_ts, aggregated_cvss_max) transformed into canonical_priority in {critical, high, medium, low} using threshold table maintained in config.

Example canonical event (fields we will emit to SIEM):
- event_type: "redwood.vuln.scan.event"
- primary_id: "CVE-2025-xxxx"
- alternate_ids: ["GHSA-...", "snyk:12345"]
- fingerprint: "sha256:..."
- asset_type: "container_image"
- asset_id: "sha256:abcdef..."
- package: "org.flib:libx:1.2.3"
- severity: "high"
- priority: "P1"
- scanner_sources: ["trivy@2026-12-01T12:10:00Z","snyk@2026-12-02T03:40:00Z"]
- evidence_refs: ["evidence://scan/1234" ]
- suggested_fix: "upgrade to >=1.2.4 or apply backport patch id BP-2026-11"
- first_seen: "2026-12-01T12:10:00Z"
- last_seen: "2026-12-08T09:20:00Z"
- dedup_group_id: "sha256:group..."

SIEM ingest mapping notes:
- We will send normalized events to the SIEM under a new sourcetype namespace with two event schemas: scan.event and remediation.audit. SIEM mapping must be stable (field names snake_case).
- Minimum SIEM fields: timestamp, fingerprint, primary_id, asset_type, asset_id, severity, priority, status, remediation_owner, evidence_refs[], scanner_sources[].
- Enrichers: on ingest, the pipeline should attach owner/contact from asset inventory, team SLA tier (from RBAC team metadata), and current route (hosted/dedicated/private) for service impact analysis.

RBAC v2 requirements (brief):
- Roles to define:
  - vuln-observer: read-only access to normalized events and SIEM dashboards (no evidence download).
  - vuln-handler: create/update remediation tasks, upload evidence, transition statuses (assign, start, remediation-verified).
  - vuln-admin: manage canonical rules, whitelist/false-positive marking, and push config changes to normalization service.
- RBAC enforcement points:
  - API layer that serves remediation ticket operations must validate role membership via identity provider claims and scope (org/team).
  - Evidence access must respect sensitivity tags (sensitive_evidence=true requires additional clearance).

Audit log schema (redwood.vuln.remediation.audit):
- Required audit fields (structured, emitted for each state transition):
  - action_type (string) e.g. "assign","status_change","evidence_upload","sla_override"
  - actor (string) user id/email
  - target_fingerprint (string)
  - target_primary_id (string)
  - prev_status (string)
  - new_status (string)
  - timestamp (ISO8601)
  - request_id (uuid)
  - evidence_ids (list of strings)
  - comment (string)
- We should ensure every remediation action results in an audit event stored in both the SIEM and a tamper-evident audit store (append-only).

Evidence automation runbook (sketch):
- When a normalized scan.event with priority P1/P0 is received:
  1) auto-create remediation ticket if no open ticket for fingerprint exists. Ticket template populated with primary_id, suggested_fix, routes, and linked asset owners.
  2) kick off an evidence-collector job: 
     - for container images: collect registry manifest, image layers list, declared licenses, and signing metadata (if available).
     - for hosts: attach last-known package-list snapshot and relevant package manager metadata.
     - for deps: attach sbom excerpt and dependency tree trimmed to the vulnerable path.
  3) evidence artifacts stored under evidence-bucket/{fingerprint}/{scan_ts}/ with metadata.json. The collector emits evidence_ids back into the remediation ticket and audit log.
  4) SLA timer starts from first_seen or ticket creation (rules configurable per team).

Patch SLA model (recommended defaults):
- P0/Critical: detect-to-patch <= 24h (hotfix capacity), auto-rollback policy if deploy impacts detected.
- P1/High: detect-to-mitigate <= 72h, detect-to-patch <= 14 days.
- P2/Medium: detect-to-mitigate <= 7 days, detect-to-patch <= 30 days.
- P3/Low: best-effort; monthly backlog review.
Notes: SLAs are applied based on canonical_priority, but RBAC team metadata can increase severity (e.g., compliance-scoped services).

Remediation lifecycle states (canonical): open -> triaged -> in_progress -> mitigated -> verified -> closed. Each transition must emit a remediation.audit event.

Edge cases & heuristics:
- Image name collisions: if a scanner reports an image tag without digest, do not create final fingerprint until resolver returns an immutable id; create a provisional-event with status provisional=true.
- False positives: provide a whitelist mechanism keyed by fingerprint; whitelist markings are only allowed by vuln-admin and must be recorded in audit store with rationale.
- Cross-scanner TTL: if a vulnerability disappears from all configured scanners for >=30 days, mark last_seen and consider auto-close with audit event.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Which concrete mechanism do we use for tamper-evident audit storage? (suggestions: write to a dedicated append-only bucket with signed manifests or push hashed events to an external ledger service).
- Should evidence artifacts be encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys for private deployments? (affects on-prem collector design).
- How aggressively do we canonicalize line numbers/stack traces for binary scanner outputs without losing actionable context?

Operational knobs and observability: 
- Expose metrics: normalization_rate, dedup_ratio, scaffold_provisional_count, evidence_collection_fail_rate.
- Dashboards: top dedup groups, SLA burn-down per-team, outstanding provisional events.
- Alerts: evidence collection failures for P0/P1, normalization service error rate >1% per hour, SIEM ingest backlog > 5k events.

Next steps (short backlog):
- P0: prototype normalization library and run on last 7 days of scanner data to estimate dedup reduction (owner: Daniel).
- P1: add SIEM field mapping and a demo ingest to staging SIEM using 500 normalized events (owner: Priya).
- P1: propose RBAC v2 role changes and required claim mappings to identity (owner: Maya).
- P2: implement evidence-collector adapters for registry and host (owner: Liam).
- P2: draft SOP for SLA enforcement and incident playbook integration (owner: Ava).

Appendix: quick normalizer pseudo logic (informal)
1) ingest raw_scan_event
2) extract candidate_ids = {cve, ghsa, osv, scanner_id}
3) primary_id = choose_authoritative(candidate_ids)
4) asset_canonical = resolve_asset(raw_event.asset)
5) canonical_key = join([primary_id, asset_canonical.type, asset_canonical.id, normalize_location(raw_event)])
6) fingerprint = sha256(canonical_key)
7) lookup existing_fingerprint in dedup_index -> if hit, merge sources and update last_seen; else create new canonical event and emit to SIEM.

Notes to reviewers: this is intended as a living proposal. Feedback: please comment inline in Confluence page SEC-VULN-FRAMEWORK-124 and link any relevant JIRA issues.

-- Ava
